questions.question:
Identify the **correct passive voice** form of the following sentence:

"Habits also have a powerful impact on our behaviors."

options.text: Our behaviors are powerfully impacted by habits.
A powerful impact is also had on our behaviors by habits.
Our behaviors have been impacted powerfully by habits.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
 
• In the active voice, the sentence is: "Habits also have a powerful impact on our behaviors."
 
• To convert to passive voice: Identify the object "a powerful impact" and place it at the beginning.
 
• Change the active verb form "have" (simple present) to its passive form "is had" (is + past participle).
 
• Maintain the adverb "also" and the prepositional phrase "on our behaviors."
 
• Add the preposition "by" followed by the original subject "habits."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"A powerful impact is also had on our behaviors by habits."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: **"Our behaviors are powerfully impacted by habits." – This changes the noun "impact" into a verb, which alters the original sentence structure rather than performing a direct voice conversion of the verb "have."
 
• **Option 3: **"Our behaviors have been impacted powerfully by habits." – Incorrect tense (present perfect) and changes the main verb.
 
• **Option 4: **"Habits impact our behaviors powerfully." – This is still in the active voice and changes the original grammatical structure.

questions.question:
Choose the **correct indirect speech** conversion of the sentence.

"Scientists say, 'Habits emerge because the brain is constantly looking for ways to save effort'".

options.text: Scientists say that habits emerge because the brain is constantly looking for ways to save effort.
Scientists said that habits emerged because the brain was constantly looking for ways to save effort.
Scientists say habits had emerged because the brain constantly looked for ways to save effort.
Scientists have said that habits emerge as the brain constantly looks for ways to save effort.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** Scientists say that habits emerge because the brain is constantly looking for ways to save effort.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **Reporting Verb in Present Tense:**
 
 
• The reporting verb **"say"** is in the present tense. According to grammar rules, if the reporting verb is in the present, future, or present perfect tense, the tense of the verbs in the reported speech does not change.
 
 
 
• **Universal Truth/Scientific Fact:**
 
 
• The statement *"Habits emerge because the brain is constantly looking for ways to save effort"* is a **scientific fact**. Scientific facts and general truths typically remain in the present tense when reported, even if the reporting verb is in the past tense.
 
 
 
• **Conjunction:**
 
 
• The conjunction **"that"** is used to introduce the reported clause in an assertive sentence.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• Quotation marks and the comma following the reporting verb are removed.
 
• The sentence ends with a simple full stop.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Scientists say that habits emerge because the brain is constantly looking for ways to save effort."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** "Scientists said that habits emerged because the brain was constantly looking for ways to save effort." 

 
 
• Incorrect because it unnecessarily changes the reporting verb to the past tense ("said") and shifts the scientific fact into the past tense ("emerged," "was looking").
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "Scientists say habits had emerged because the brain constantly looked for ways to save effort." 
 
 
• Incorrect because it uses the past perfect ("had emerged") and simple past ("looked"), which alters the original meaning and violates the rule for present-tense reporting verbs.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "Scientists have said that habits emerge as the brain constantly looks for ways to save effort." 
 
 
• Incorrect because it changes the reporting verb to the present perfect ("have said") and modifies the original sentence structure (replacing "because" with "as").

questions.question:
Choose the best synonym for the word "trigger" in the sentence:

"The cue is the trigger that tells your brain to go into automatic mode."
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 2** i.e. initiator.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"trigger"** means:

 
 
• An event or situation that causes something to start; something that sets off a process or initiates an action. (ट्रिगर)
 
 
 
• In the sentence provided, "The cue is the trigger that tells your brain to go into automatic mode," "trigger" implies something that initiates or starts the brain's automatic response.
 
• **Initiator** means a person or thing that initiates someone or something. (आरंभकर्ता)
 
• **Example:** The initiator of the movement was awarded for their efforts.

Therefore, the best synonym for "trigger" in the given sentence is: **initiator.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options and their meanings:

• **Example:** The barrier blocked the entrance to the restricted area.
 
 
 
• **Obstacle** (अवरोध): A thing that blocks one's way or prevents or hinders progress.
 
 
• **Example:** The construction work created an obstacle on the road.
 
 
 
• **Conclusion** (निष्कर्ष): The end or finish of an event, process, or text.
 
 
• **Example:** The conclusion of the meeting was very productive.

questions.question: According to the passage, why does the brain try to turn routines into habits?

options.text: Because habits help conserve mental effort, making survival easier.
Because habits make the brain grow larger and more powerful.
Because habits prevent the brain from making automatic decisions.
Because habits eliminate the need for learning new things.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 1**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***A) The Brain's Effort-Saving Instinct:***

 
 
• The passage explicitly states that the brain is **"constantly looking for ways to save effort."** Habits are the primary tool the brain uses to achieve this because they allow the mind to "ramp down" and require less active processing power.
 
 
 
• ***B) Evolutionary and Survival Advantages:***
 
 
• The text connects mental efficiency to biological survival. An efficient brain requires **"less room,"** which historically led to smaller heads, making **childbirth easier** and survival for the species more likely.
 
 
 
• ***C) Automaticity:***
 
 
• By turning routines into habits, the brain allows behaviors to **"operate automatically."** This frees up mental resources for other tasks, reinforcing the "effort-saving" goal mentioned at the beginning of the text.
 
 

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2**: Incorrect because the passage states the opposite—an efficient brain (powered by habits) requires **"less room,"** not more.
 
• **Option 3**: Incorrect because the passage says habits **enable** automatic mode (via the "cue"), rather than preventing it.
 
• **Option 4**: Incorrect because while habits make routines easier, the passage does not suggest they **eliminate** the need for new learning; rather, it says understanding the habit loop allows us to **change or create** new habits.

questions.question: Which term refers to: "A narrative technique that involves a backward shift in the chronology of the story, where the plot jumps to an earlier time in the character's life."
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **1) Analepsis**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term **"Analepsis"** refers to a narrative technique where the plot shifts backward in time to recount earlier events in a character's life. (पूर्वगमन)
 
 
• **Example:** In the novel "Wuthering Heights," the story begins in the present but frequently uses analepsis to narrate events from the past.
 
 
• This technique is commonly referred to as a "flashback" in literature and cinema. It is used to provide background information and context to the main storyline.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Analepsis**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Prolepsis** (पूर्वाभास): A narrative technique that involves a forward shift in the chronology of the story, often used to foreshadow future events.
 
 
• **Example:** "In the years to come, this decision would prove to be pivotal." This sentence is an example of prolepsis.
 
 
 
• **Flashback** (फ्लैशबैक): A popular term used to describe analepsis, where past events are revisited in a narrative. This makes it synonymous with "analepsis."
 
 
• **Example:** The character vividly remembers her childhood during a flashback scene in the movie.
 
 
 
• **Foreshadowing** (पूर्वसंकेत): A literary device where hints or clues about future events in the story are provided.
 
 
• **Example:** The dark clouds gathering in the sky foreshadowed the storm that was about to come.

questions.question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:

By the time the audit team (1)/ reaches the headquarters (2)/ the financial report (3)/ would already be submitted. (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary error in the sentence lies in the tense usage in **part 4**.
 
• The phrase "**By the time**" followed by a simple present verb ("reaches") indicates a deadline in the future.
 
• To describe an action that will be completed before a specific point in the future, the **Future Perfect Tense** ($will + have + past participle$) must be used.
 
• Since the "financial report" is receiving the action, it requires the passive voice: "**will have already been submitted**."
 
• Thus, the error is located in **part 4** of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"By the time the audit team **reaches the headquarters the financial report will have already been** submitted."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **1: "By the time the audit team"** – This part is grammatically correct as it sets up the time clause.
 
• **2: "reaches the headquarters"** – In "by the time" constructions referring to the future, the time clause correctly uses the Simple Present tense.
 
• **3: "the financial report"** – This is the correct subject for the following main clause.
 
• **"Would" vs "Will"** – "Would" is used for hypothetical or past-future contexts, whereas "will" is necessary here for a factual future completion.

Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:

The manager insisted that (1)/ every member completes (2)/ the survey before (3)/ the deadline expired. (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error is in **part 2** of the sentence due to the incorrect verb form "**completes**."
 
• The verb "**insisted**" is a verb of requirement or demand. When such verbs (e.g., insist, suggest, demand, mandate) are followed by "**that**," they trigger the **Subjunctive Mood**.
 
• In the subjunctive mood, the **base form** of the verb (the infinitive without "to") is used for all subjects, regardless of whether the subject is singular or plural.
 
• Therefore, "completes" should be replaced with "**complete**."
 
• Thus, the error is located in **part 2** of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The manager insisted that **every member complete** the survey before the deadline expired."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **1: "The manager insisted that"** – This part is correct; it establishes the demand that triggers the change in the following clause.
 
• **3: "the survey before"** – This part is grammatically correct as it provides the object and the preposition for the time condition.
 
• **4: "the deadline expired."** – This part is correct. In a past-tense narrative (insisted), the use of "expired" maintains the sequence of events in the past.
 
• **Subjunctive Rule:** Even though "every member" is singular, the subjunctive mood ignores the standard "-s" ending used in the present indicative tense.

questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option:
Among the shortlisted candidates, she presented the ___ argument with impeccable logic and evidence.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**most compelling**'. 
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 
__ 
 
• The blank requires an adjective that describes the argument presented by the candidate in the most effective manner. 
 
• **Option 1: "most compelling"** is correct as it is a superlative form used to indicate the highest degree of comparison and fits the context perfectly. 
 
• **Option 2: "more compelling"** is incorrect because it is a comparative form, which is used to compare two arguments, but there is no such comparison in the given sentence. 
 
• **Option 3: "much compelling"** is grammatically incorrect as "much" does not correctly modify the adjective "compelling." 
 
• **Option 4: "most compelled"** is incorrect because "compelled" is a past participle and does not describe the quality of the argument in this context. 
 
Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**. 
 
**Complete Sentence:** *"Among the shortlisted candidates, she presented the **most compelling**__ argument with impeccable logic and evidence."* 
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** 
 
 
• **Superlative Adjective:** Superlatives are used to describe the highest degree of a quality among three or more options. They are often preceded by "the." 
 
• **Example:** She is the most intelligent student in the class. 
 
• **Comparative Adjective:** Comparatives are used to compare two options. For example, "She is more intelligent than her friend."

questions.question:
**Change the following from active to passive:**

The ethics committee will be evaluating the implications of the findings over the next quarter.

options.text: The implications of the findings will be being evaluated by the ethics committee over the next quarter.
The findings' implications were evaluated by the committee over the next quarter.
The implications will have been evaluated by the committee over the next quarter.
The committee would be evaluating the implications over the next quarter.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence is in the **Future Continuous Tense** (will be + evaluating).
 
• To convert a Future Continuous sentence into the passive voice, the structure is: **Object + will + be + being + Past Participle (V3) + by + Subject**.
 
• In this sentence, the object "**the implications of the findings**" becomes the subject, and the verb "**evaluating**" becomes "**being evaluated**."
 
• Option 1 correctly follows this grammatical structure, making it the accurate passive transformation.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Passive Sentence:** *"The implications of the findings **will be being evaluated by the ethics** committee over the next quarter."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** Uses the **Past Simple Passive** ("were evaluated"), which changes the timeframe from the future to the past.
 
• **Option 3:** Uses the **Future Perfect Passive** ("will have been evaluated"), which implies the action will be finished by a certain time, rather than ongoing.
 
• **Option 4:** Changes the mood to **Conditional** ("would be evaluating") and remains in the active voice, which does not satisfy the requirement.

questions.question:
Convert the sentence provided below from its passive voice structure to an active voice structure:

The project is being evaluated by the panel.

options.text: The panel was evaluating the project.
The panel has evaluated the project.
The panel is evaluating the project.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence is in the **Present Continuous Passive** voice ("is being evaluated").
 
• To convert it to the **active voice**, the object of the passive sentence ("the panel") becomes the subject of the active sentence.
 
• The verb structure must change from *is/am/are + being + V3* to **is/am/are + V1+ing** to maintain the continuous tense.
 
• Therefore, "is being evaluated" becomes "**is evaluating**."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The panel **is evaluating** the project."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "The panel was evaluating the project."** – This is in the Past Continuous tense, which changes the original meaning.
 
• **Option 2: "The panel has evaluated the project."** – This is in the Present Perfect tense, indicating a completed action.
 
• **Option 4: "The panel evaluates the project."** – This is in the Simple Present tense, which indicates a general fact or habit rather than an ongoing action.

questions.question:
Convert the sentence provided below from its passive voice structure to an active voice structure:

The security protocols had been overlooked by the administration prior to the incident.

options.text: The administration has overlooked the security protocols prior to the incident.
The administration overlooks the security protocols prior to the incident.
The administration was overlooking the security protocols prior to the incident.
The administration had overlooked the security protocols prior to the incident.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence is in the **Past Perfect Passive** voice ("had been overlooked").
 
• To convert this to the **active voice**, the agent performing the action ("the administration") becomes the subject of the sentence.
 
• The verb must remain in the **Past Perfect** tense. The passive structure *had + been + V3* changes to the active structure **had + V3**.
 
• Consequently, "had been overlooked" is converted to "**had overlooked**."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The administration **had overlooked** the security protocols prior to the incident."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "The administration has overlooked..."** – This uses the Present Perfect tense, which incorrectly shifts the timeline to the present.
 
• **Option 2: "The administration overlooks..."** – This uses the Simple Present tense, which describes a general habit or fact rather than a past event.
 
• **Option 3: "The administration was overlooking..."** – This uses the Past Continuous tense, which describes an ongoing action in the past rather than a completed state/action.

questions.question:
A sentence is provided in direct speech. From the four given options, choose the one that most accurately conveys the sentence in its corresponding indirect speech.

“Though the facts were evident, the jury chose to ignore them,” he observed.

options.text: He observed the facts had been evident, but jury ignored them.
He observed that though the facts had been evident, the jury had chosen to ignore them.
He observed though facts were evident, jury ignored it.
He observed that even though facts were code evident, jury ignored them.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** He observed that though the facts had been evident, the jury had chosen to ignore them.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **Reporting Verb in Past Tense:**
 
 
• The reporting verb **"observed"** is in the past tense. When the reporting verb is in the past, the tenses within the reported speech must undergo **backshifting** (moving one step back into the past).
 
 
 
• **Tense Changes (Backshifting):**
 
 
• The simple past **"were"** changes to the past perfect **"had been"**.
 
• The simple past **"chose"** changes to the past perfect **"had chosen"**.
 
 
 
• **Conjunction:**
 
 
• The conjunction **"that"** is used to connect the reporting clause with the reported speech.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• Quotation marks and the comma separating the reporting verb are removed.
 
• The sentence structure maintains the subordinating conjunction **"though"** to preserve the original meaning.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"He observed that though the facts had been evident, the jury had chosen to ignore them."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "He observed the facts had been evident, but jury ignored them." 

 
 
• Incorrect because it changes the conjunction from **"though"** to **"but"** and fails to backshift **"ignored"**. It also lacks the necessary article "the" before "jury".
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "He observed though facts were evident, jury ignored it." 
 
 
• Incorrect because it lacks tense backshifting, misses articles, and uses the singular pronoun **"it"** to refer to the plural "facts".
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "He observed that even though facts were code evident, jury ignored them." 
 
 
• Incorrect due to the nonsensical phrase **"code evident"** (a likely typo), missing articles, and a lack of proper tense backshifting.

questions.question:
A sentence is provided in indirect speech. From the four given options, choose the one that most accurately conveys the sentence in its corresponding direct speech.

The professor reminded the students that if they had not registered on the portal by midnight, their submissions would not be accepted.

options.text: “Your submissions will not be accepted if you don’t register by midnight,” the professor reminded them.
“If you haven’t registered by midnight, your work won’t be accepted,” the professor warned.
“Register on the portal by midnight or your submissions will be rejected,” the professor said.
“If you fail to register by midnight, your submissions won’t be accepted,” said the professor.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** The professor reminded the students that if they had not registered on the portal by midnight, their submissions would not be accepted.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **Reporting Verb Match:**
 
 
• The indirect speech uses the reporting verb **"reminded"**. Option 1 is the only choice that maintains this specific reporting verb, preserving the tone and intent of the original sentence.
 
 
 
• **Tense Backshifting (Reversed):**
 
 
• **"would not be accepted"** (Future-in-the-past) in indirect speech converts back to **"will not be accepted"** (Future) in direct speech.
 
• **"had not registered"** (Past Perfect) in indirect speech often acts as the reported version of a **present/past condition**. In this context, it refers to the requirement **"don’t register"** (Present Simple) or "haven't registered," emphasizing the consequence.
 
 
 
• **Pronoun Change:**
 
 
• The third-person pronouns **"they"** and **"their"** in indirect speech are converted back to the second-person pronouns **"you"** and **"your"** to reflect the professor addressing the students directly.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• The direct speech is enclosed in quotation marks.
 
• The comma separates the quoted statement from the reporting clause.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"“Your submissions will not be accepted if you don’t register by midnight,” the professor reminded them."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** "If you haven’t registered by midnight, your work won’t be accepted,” the professor warned."

 
 
• While the tenses are grammatically plausible, it changes the reporting verb to **"warned"** and changes "submissions" to "work."
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "Register on the portal by midnight or your submissions will be rejected,” the professor said."
 
 
• This converts the conditional "if" clause into an imperative sentence, which changes the original grammatical structure and reporting verb.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "If you fail to register by midnight, your submissions won’t be accepted,” said the professor."
 
 
• Changes the verb "register" to the phrase "fail to register" and uses the generic reporting verb "said" instead of the specific "reminded."

questions.question:
Rearrange the following sentences in correct order to make a meaningful sentence

P: is urgently needed

Q: to prevent the misuse of user data

R: a comprehensive framework

S: for digital privacy laws
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option (2)** i.e. **RSPQ**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence begins with the primary subject **"A comprehensive framework,"** which is indicated by **part (R).**
 
• Following the subject, the prepositional phrase **"for digital privacy laws" (S)** is needed to specify what the framework is intended for, creating the complete subject phrase **(RS).**
 
• **The next part,** **"is urgently needed" (P),** provides the main verb and predicate, establishing the necessity of the framework.
 
• **Ending with** the infinitive phrase **"to prevent the misuse of user data" (Q)** provides the logical purpose or reason behind the urgency, completing the thought.

Therefore, the correct sequence is **RSPQ.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1 (PRSQ):** Starts with the verb "is urgently needed," which leaves the sentence without a proper introductory subject in this context.
 
• **Option 3 (RPQS):** While "A comprehensive framework is urgently needed" is grammatically okay, placing "to prevent the misuse of user data" before "for digital privacy laws" creates a confusing link between "user data" and "laws."
 
• **Option 4 (QSRP):** This sequence results in "To prevent the misuse of user data for digital privacy laws a comprehensive framework is urgently needed," which incorrectly implies the data belongs to the laws rather than the users.
